newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM precious metals end mixed, volume moderate.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM precious metals end mixed, volume moderate.

text.p: Tokyo precious metal futures ended mixed on Monday, pressured by the yen's firmness against the dollar, traders said.
Gold futures ranged from four yen to eight yen per gram lower. Benchmark February was off five yen at 1,373 yen.
Platinum futures, except for the spot April contract, were weaker in a correction after a sharp rise in bullion prices late last week on concerns over Russian metal supplies.
Platinum futures ranged from five yen per gram lower to 13 yen up. Benchmark February platinum was off two yen per gram at 1,471 yen.
Spot gold was quoted at $342.10/40 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against $341.10/60 in New York on Friday.
In gold futures, private investors hunted for bargains, while trade houses bought spot gold in arbitrage trade.
Trade in platinum and palladium futures was cautious amid uncertainty as to when Russian platinum group metal shipments would resume.
A source in Japan said Russian central bank officials are to meet with some Japanese trade houses this week to discuss the possible use of gold to back bonds issued by the Russian government.
Some traders suggested they are likely to raise the issue of delayed platinum group metal shipments at the meeting.
Platinum short-term lease rates, the cost of borrowing the metal, jumped to around 13 percent on Monday, reflecting a tightening of the spot Zurich market, the traders said.
Palladium lease rates also remained at high levels of around 10 percent.
Silver futures ended mostly firmer, reflecting firmer spot prices, the traders said. Benchmark February silver was up 0.1 yen per 10 grams at 193.1 yen.
